title: Finding
description: One record per (population, intervention, comparator, endpoint, timepoint). A PAPER IS NOT A FINDING: the extraction prompt already asks for a primary outcome, a secondary_outcomes list and 3-5 key findings (clinical.py:2420,2430), so one paper routinely reports benefit on one endpoint and a null result on another. Hanging a singular direction/value off the paper-level DeepExtraction forces an arbitrary pick and silently discards the rest, which breaks replication grouping and the ordered claim records the translation audit needs. Smart proposes the values; Python computes finding_key and validates the schema, the locator coverage and the literal spans; Claude verifies attribution.

finding_key.description: sha1 of the normalised (population, intervention, comparator, endpoint, timepoint) tuple. COMPUTED BY PYTHON, never authored by the model — a model-authored key makes replication grouping a semantic task again, which is the defect the key exists to remove. schemas.compute_finding_key() is the only producer, and the validator rejects any record whose key does not match it.

timepoint.description: Follow-up timepoint the result is reported at, e.g. '12週'. null when the design has none (cross-sectional); null and absent are the same identity for finding_key purposes.

direction.description: Direction of the effect on this endpoint. Never inferable from a hedge phrase — 効果が確認された and 効果が確認されなかった carry the same hedge token and opposite meanings.

is_primary.description: True iff this is the paper's pre-specified primary outcome.

control_event_rate.description: CER as a proportion in [0,1]. Consumed per-finding by clinical_math.calculate_impact().

outcome_is_adverse.description: True = the counted event is bad. PER-FINDING, not per-paper: clinical_math.py:39 flips the ARR direction on this flag, so a paper reporting one beneficial and one adverse endpoint would otherwise apply a single polarity to both and produce a directionally wrong NNT.

locators.description: Field-level provenance. Every claim-bearing field that is non-null must be named by at least one entry, and no entry may name a field that is null — see schemas.CLAIM_BEARING_FIELDS. Coverage is enforced in Python because JSON Schema cannot express it.
